body: Adds vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid() check before accessing window buffers to prevent errors when window IDs become invalid, such as with empty folders.

comment_regular_data.body:
Thanks for the PR!

> ... to prevent errors when window IDs become invalid, such as with empty folders.

Could you please elaborate on this? How can I (and future test) reproduce this error?

Admittedly most of the time I get this error is due to an autocmd I set up on MiniFilesWindowUpdate which calls MiniFiles.get_explorer_state() but I believe this could happen in other situations.

Occasionally there will be an invalid window id and it causes an error. I noticed this mostly when working on Windows. You can ignore the empty folders comment, I did some more testing and I discovered that previewing files where you don't have read access causes the error consistently.

So to repro:
Use Windows (sorry)
Set up an autocmd on MiniFilesWindowUpdate that calls MiniFiles.get_explorer_state()
Try to preview a file like a system file where you don't have read access.

> You can ignore the empty folders comment, I did some more testing and I discovered that previewing files where you don't have read access causes the error consistently.

I think this might be the culprit that is worth fixing.

'mini.files' already [does the check](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/ca9adcfc4e796b292cc9072f4952318ef5a7f6c0/lua/mini/files.lua#L2310-L2311) of whether a file is readable, which I thought was enough.

As I don't have Windows access, could you please test on Windows for the file without read access:
- `:=vim.uv.fs_open('unreadable-file', 'r', 1)` . I think it should show `nil`.
- `:=vim.fn.filereadable('unreadable-file')` . I think it should show 0.

Also, could you try applying the following patch and see if it fixes the initial problem you have:

```diff
diff --git a/lua/mini/files.lua b/lua/mini/files.lua
index 331bead2..bee195e2 100644
--- a/lua/mini/files.lua
+++ b/lua/mini/files.lua
@@ -2305,6 +2305,9 @@ H.buffer_update_directory = function(buf_id, path, opts, is_preview)
 end

+  if vim.fn.filereadable(path) == 0 then
+    return H.set_buflines(buf_id, { '-No-access' .. string.rep('-', opts.windows.width_preview) })
+  end

   -- Source: https://github.com/sharkdp/content_inspector

```

The patch doesn't fix the problem. I don't think that early return there would fix the problem even if filereadable returned 0 correctly. I tried setting the compare value to 1 just to see and I still got the error.

Ok I dug further and found the culprit.

With preview enabled in C:/, hovering files like:
DumpStack.log.tmp
pagefile.sys
swapfile.sys

shows -No-fs-entry-, and trying to open them says they don’t exist. But they do exist, they’re just protected/locked by Windows.

In these cases vim.loop.fs_stat() returns nil, so fs_is_present_path() treats them as not present. That makes fs_get_type() return nil, which leads to -No-fs-entry-. Feels like we should distinguish:

truly missing: -No-fs-entry-

present but inaccessible: -No-access-

One fix that worked for me is: if fs_stat() fails on Windows, fall back to scanning the parent dir for the basename:

```lua
H.fs_is_present_path = function(path)
  if H.fs_is_imaginary_path(path) then return false end
  if vim.loop.fs_stat(path) ~= nil then return true end

  if H.is_windows then
    local parent = H.fs_get_parent(path)
    if not parent then return false end

    local base = H.fs_get_basename(path)
    local fs = vim.loop.fs_scandir(parent)
    if not fs then return false end

    while true do
      local name = vim.loop.fs_scandir_next(fs)
      if not name then break end
      if name == base then return true end
    end
  end

  return false
end
```

This also seemed related to the “invalid win_id” I was seeing: MiniFilesWindowUpdate can fire mid-refresh (called inside H.explorer_refresh_depth_window()), so explorer.windows isn’t necessarily stable if an integration calls get_explorer_state() right there. If that’s expected, maybe a MiniFilesRefreshComplete event at the end of H.explorer_refresh() would give integrations a safe point to do layout/state work without vim.schedule().

```diff

index 331bead2..424934b7 100644
--- a/lua/mini/files.lua
+++ b/lua/mini/files.lua
@@ -2638,6 +2638,11 @@ end

 H.fs_is_present_path = function(path) return vim.loop.fs_stat(path) ~= nil and not H.fs_is_imaginary_path(path) end
+if H.is_windows then
+  H.fs_is_present_path = function(path)
+    return (vim.loop.fs_stat(path) ~= nil or vim.fn.filereadable(path) == 1) and not H.fs_is_imaginary_path(path)

+end
 
 H.fs_child_path = function(dir, name) return H.fs_normalize_path(string.format('%s/%s', dir, name)) end
 
```

@TheLeoP, as I don't have Windows, could you also please take a deeper dive here and in the other issue you noticed?

As far as I can tell, the issue comes from the fact that the root path `C:/` is being normalized as `C:/C:`, so 

https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/ca9adcfc4e796b292cc9072f4952318ef5a7f6c0/lua/mini/files.lua#L2669

returns `false` and `mini.files` tries to go up a directory, failing to do so. I even think that the lack of access to a file is a red hearing, as I can reproduce the original issue without hovering such a file.

This happens because

https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/ca9adcfc4e796b292cc9072f4952318ef5a7f6c0/lua/mini/files.lua#L2634-L2636

normalizes `C:\\` as `C:` (removing the trailing slash because of the pattern in the last `:gsub('(.)[\\/]$', '%1')`, which doesn't happen for Linux because `/` does not match the equivalent `gsub('(.)/$', '%1')`) which isn't recognized as the top level directory and then gets expanded to `C:/C:`.

Removing the last `gsub` (as a proof of concept, because it should be fixed instead to work in all cases) does indeed remove the issue for me @echasnovski

I made an AI slop robust function and this fixes all the errors. I can try to make something that's less lines of code once I have time if that helps.
```lua
if H.is_windows then
  H.fs_normalize_path = function(path)
    if type(path) ~= 'string' or path == '' then return path end

    -- 1) Normalize separators
    path = path:gsub('\\', '/')

    -- 2) Extended-length / device paths (keep the prefix exactly)
    --    \\?\C:\foo  -> //?/C:/foo
    --    \\.\COM1    -> //./COM1
    if path:sub(1, 4) == '//?/' or path:sub(1, 4) == '//./' then
      local prefix = path:sub(1, 4)
      local rest = path:sub(5)
      -- collapse slashes in rest
      rest = rest:gsub('/+', '/')
      -- strip trailing slash unless the rest is empty (just the prefix)
      if rest ~= '' then rest = rest:gsub('/+$', '') end
      return prefix .. rest
    end

    -- 3) UNC paths (must keep the initial double slash)
    --    \\server\share -> //server/share
    if path:sub(1, 2) == '//' then
      local rest = path:sub(3)
      rest = rest:gsub('^/+', '') -- don't allow more than 2 leading slashes total
      rest = rest:gsub('/+', '/')
      rest = rest:gsub('/+$', '')
      return '//' .. rest
    end

    -- 4) Drive-letter paths
    -- Absolute:  C:\Users -> C:/Users
    -- Root:      C:\ or C:// -> preserve root form
    -- Relative:  C:foo  (leave as C:foo, but still normalize slashes inside)
    if path:match('^[A-Za-z]:') then
      local drive = path:sub(1, 2) -- "C:"
      local rest = path:sub(3) -- includes whatever after "C:"

      -- If it looks absolute/rooted (next char was a slash), keep exactly one slash
      if rest:sub(1, 1) == '/' then
        -- preserve "C://..." (if user provided multiple slashes right after the colon)
        local m = rest:match('^(/*)')
        local lead = m or '/'
        local tail = rest:sub(#lead + 1)

        tail = tail:gsub('/+', '/') -- collapse internal doubles
        -- trailing slash rules: keep drive root slashes, strip otherwise
        if tail == '' then
          return drive .. lead -- e.g. "C:/" or "C://"
        else
          tail = tail:gsub('/+$', '')
          return drive .. lead .. tail
        end
      else
        -- Relative drive path (C:foo). Normalize inside but don't invent a slash.
        rest = rest:gsub('/+', '/')
        rest = rest:gsub('/+$', '')
        return drive .. rest
      end
    end

    -- 5) Posix-ish paths
    -- Preserve leading "/" (root), collapse duplicates, strip trailing unless root.
    local is_root = (path == '/') or (path:match('^/+$') ~= nil)
    if is_root then return '/' end

    local leading = path:sub(1, 1) == '/' and '/' or ''
    local rest = leading == '/' and path:sub(2) or path

    rest = rest:gsub('/+', '/')
    rest = rest:gsub('/+$', '')

    return leading .. rest
  end
end
```

I've changed this PR to reflect the root cause of the issue and also committed my solution for the issue.

```lua
if H.is_windows then
  H.fs_normalize_path = function(path)
    path = path:gsub('\\', '/'):gsub('///+', '//')
    local prefix = path:sub(1, 2)
    local rest = path:sub(3):gsub('/+', '/'):gsub('/+$', '')
    if prefix:match('%a:') then prefix = prefix .. '/' end
    return prefix .. rest
  end
end
```
This new function handles UNC and Extended-length paths (starting with //) and also gives improved behavior with forward slashes after drive letters. I've tested it and it's resolved all of my issues.

Thank you both for taking a closer look!

As far as I understand, the summary for problematic Windows path normalization is:
- For `C://` path it should preserve trailing slash(es). All of [this](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/pull/2272#issuecomment-3931219484), #2277, and built-in `vim.fs.normalize()` result in `C:/`.
- The `C://file` should be `C://file`.
- The `C:///file` should reduce the number of slashes. Probably, to `C://file`.
- It should not matter whether `/` or `\` is used.

The hypothetical questions is: should `C:/file` (one slash) be normalized as `C://file`? My hope and general logic says "no". Plus Neovim's `vim.fs.fnamemodify(path, ':p')` and later `vim.fs.abspath()` might already result in paths with `C:\\` and not `C:\`.

The current implementation in this PR does always ensure `C://` even if the input starts only with `C:/`.

---

Taking into account that `:` is a not supported filename character on Windows, I have a possibly more concise solution.

```diff
diff --git a/lua/mini/files.lua b/lua/mini/files.lua
index 331bead2..78b8f185 100644
--- a/lua/mini/files.lua
+++ b/lua/mini/files.lua
@@ -2632,7 +2632,9 @@ end
 
 H.fs_normalize_path = function(path) return (path:gsub('/+', '/'):gsub('(.)/$', '%1')) end
 if H.is_windows then
-  H.fs_normalize_path = function(path) return (path:gsub('\\', '/'):gsub('([^/])/+', '%1/'):gsub('(.)[\\/]$', '%1')) end
+  H.fs_normalize_path = function(path)
+    return (path:gsub('\\', '/'):gsub('([^/:])/+', '%1/'):gsub('([^:])/+$', '%1'):gsub('^(%a):/+([^/])', '%1://%2'))
+  end
 end
 
 H.fs_is_imaginary_path = function(path) return path:sub(-1) == '\000' end
```

@nickvonkaenel and @TheLeoP, could you please test this approach and see if it fixes the issues you separately found?

---

Side notes:
- 'mini.files' does not use `vim.fs.normalize` for better performance.
- All online documentation says that `C:/file` should work just fine and there should be no need for `C://file` (which is somewhat incorrect even). So maybe this is partially a `libuv` issue and forcing `C://` in file paths is wrong and only `C://` -> `C:/` should be taken into account.

    I would appreciate also testing the variant of the above patch with `gsub('^(%a):/+([^/])', '%1:/%2')` as the last `gsub`. I.e. to ensure a `/` and not `//` as the volume prefix.

> could you please test this approach and see if it fixes the issues you separately found? If fixes all of the issues I found. It even (maybe unintentionally?) solves the issue @nickvonkaenel mentioned about `MiniFiles.reveal_cwd()` (that is also an issue with #2277). > I would appreciate also testing the variant of the above patch with `gsub('^(%a):/+([^/])', '%1:/%2')` as the last `gsub`. I.e. to ensure a `/` and not `//` as the volume prefix. I'm seeing the error that I mentioned in https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/pull/2277#issuecomment-3930589118 with this change. I also realized that it only happens if the explorer gets in a state where `explorer.branch` looks like `{ "C://", "C:/vfcompat.dll" }` (the root must have 2 trailing slashes for the error to happen), the cursor is moved on top of a files that requires `C://` and then on top of a file that doesn't require it. I can reliably get the explorer to said state by ` :lua MiniFiles.open('C:/vfcompat.dll')` where `vfcompat.dll` is any file under `C:/` that does not require `C://` (weirdly enough). It also doesn't solve the issue with `MiniFiles.reveal_cwd()` because https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/b70d9f932240b69be98ac46f1056581825ed0523/lua/mini/files.lua#L2881 has the values ``` ┆H.validate_branch#for┆ ╎(parent .. '/' .. child:match('[^/]+$'))╎: "C://$Recycle.Bin" ┆H.validate_branch#for┆ ╎res[i] ╎: "C:/$Recycle.Bin" ``` which do not match unless `C:/` is always normalized to `C://`. My guess is that that's not the intention of the code, but I don't fully understand the intended logic, so I may be wrong. --- > So maybe this is partially a libuv issue and forcing C:// in file paths is wrong and only C:// -> C:/ should be taken into account. That may be true. My empirical conclusion that certain files require `C://` came from the fact that `:edit` autocompleted them only for `C://` and not for `C:/` (and it also only gave a permission warning when trying to open them with `C://`). But Neovim may be indeed using libuv under the hood to handle file system access on the C side (? `:e c:/`, some files do not show up `:e c://` all of the files that (I think) require `C://` do show up

I can confirm what @TheLeoP is reporting. The function you provided works for me, but if I change the last gsub function then there is an error with reveal_cwd / validate_branch and 'branch contains not a parent-child pair'
Thank you both! I'll fix it soon-ish with some additional testing to ensure that this behavior on Windows persists.

All right. I've update `main` branch to follow Windows path normalization on Windows as in [this comment](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/pull/2272#issuecomment-3933044987). It required a couple of tweaks (mostly because this *does* look like not a standard way of normalizing paths, since current directory uses `C:\dir` notation). Plus there is now a (first of its kind) test of internal helper: mostly to document this conversation and make the future changes at least more educated.

@nickvonkaenel and @TheLeoP, huge thanks to you both for helping me debug this! Let's hope this change won't trigger some other problems down the road.
